newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice steady as Malaysia buys, El Nino watched.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice steady as Malaysia buys, El Nino watched.

text.p: Thai rice prices were steady to lower this week with Malaysia stepping in to buy 10,000 tonnes, traders said on Thursday.

Malaysia tendered to buy 5,000 tonnes of glutinous rice and 5,000 tonnes of 100 percent fragrant grade earlier this week but price details were not available. There were also some buying orders from Singapore, traders told Reuters.
The market was also watching closely for any developments from the El Nino effect which has increased chances of a drought across Southeast Asia, Australia and India, threatening crops.

"We are watching its impact on our traditional rice buyers such as Indonesia and the Philippines or other competitors such as the United States and India rather than on our own crops," said one exporter.
"Thailand was hardly effected by El Nino when those two countries were badly hit last time," he said.
An agriculture ministry official told Reuters the ministry would release its quarterly crop forecast next week and the rice projection would not be revised down.
The El Nino effect, a warm current of water in the Pacific, can upset global weather patterns for up to 18 months, depending on how soon ocean temperatures return to normal.
Thai benchmark 100 percent B grade was quoted around $320-360 per tonne FOB Bangkok while 100 percent fragrant grade edged down slightly to $690-710 baht.

"I see the prices moving in this range, possibly with downward bias as most shippers have covered positions and are buying hand to mouth. There are not many vessels coming in to load rice at the moment either," said another trader.
Thailand has so far exported 2.0 million tonnes of rice between January 1 and June 11 compared with 2.61 million tonnes during the same period last year.
